result.keywords: This fictional paper examines decorative wind-driven installations used in seaside public spaces, focusing on materials, motion patterns, and visitor perception rather than robotics, computing, or agricultural sensing. It proposes a simple taxonomy for ribbon arrays, reflective vanes, and suspended kinetic sculptures, and compares maintenance requirements across salt-exposed environments. A small observational study reports qualitative responses from promenade visitors and offers design guidelines for placemaking and low-energy ambience creation.
result.title: Cerulean Looms for Coastal Wind Ornamentation.
